scheme_name: PMMSY: Construction of New Grow Out Ponds - Haryana
description:
The Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) is a flagship scheme launched by the Government of India on September 10, 2020. 

This scheme aims to enhance fish production and promote sustainable aquaculture in the country. 

The PMMSY is a comprehensive scheme that focuses on various aspects of the fisheries sector. 

One of the key components of PMMSY is the construction of new grow-out ponds. 

This initiative is particularly significant in states like Haryana, where aquaculture has the potential to boost the local economy. 

The primary objective of the PMMSY is to achieve an increase in fish production to 220 lakh metric tons by 2024-2025. 

The scheme aims to provide direct and indirect employment to around 28 lakh fishers and fish farmers. 

The government has allocated a budget of ₹20,050 crores for the implementation of PMMSY over a period of five years. 

The construction of new grow-out ponds under PMMSY is designed to enhance the capacity of fish farming in Haryana. 

The scheme encourages the establishment of modern aquaculture practices to increase productivity. 

The benefits of constructing new grow-out ponds include improved fish yield and income generation for fish farmers. 

Farmers can receive financial assistance of up to 40% of the project cost for constructing new grow-out ponds. 

For Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, the financial assistance can go up to 60% of the project cost. 

The maximum project cost eligible for assistance is capped at ₹10 lakhs per beneficiary. 

The scheme is expected to significantly increase the income of fish farmers in Haryana. 

The average income of fish farmers is projected to rise by 50% due to the implementation of this scheme. 

Eligibility criteria for beneficiaries include being a registered fish farmer or a cooperative society of fish farmers. 

Applicants must be at least 18 years old to qualify for the scheme. 

The income limit for individual beneficiaries is set at ₹3 lakhs per annum. 

For cooperative societies, there is no specific income limit. 

The application process for the PMMSY scheme involves several steps. 

First, interested beneficiaries must approach the local fisheries department in Haryana. 

They need to fill out the application form provided by the department. 

Required documents include proof of identity, proof of residence, and bank account details. 

Additionally, applicants must provide a project report detailing the construction plan for the grow-out pond. 

Once the application is submitted, it will be reviewed by the fisheries department. 

If approved, beneficiaries will receive a sanction letter outlining the financial assistance. 

The disbursement of funds is typically made in installments based on the progress of the project. 

The first installment is released after the completion of the initial phase of construction. 

Subsequent installments are released upon verification of the completed work. 

The implementation of the PMMSY scheme is overseen by the Department of Fisheries under the Ministry of Fisheries Animal Husbandry and Dairying. 

The contact details for the Department of Fisheries in Haryana can be found on the official state government website. 

The scheme is expected to be implemented in a phased manner over the next five years. 

Regular monitoring and evaluation will be conducted to assess the impact of the scheme on fish production and farmers' income. 

The PMMSY also emphasizes the need for sustainable practices in aquaculture. 

This includes promoting the use of eco-friendly feed and disease management practices. 

The construction of new grow-out ponds will also contribute to the conservation of aquatic biodiversity. 

The scheme aligns with the government's vision of doubling farmers' income by 2022. 

It also supports the broader goals of the National Fisheries Policy, which aims to promote sustainable fisheries management. 

The PMMSY is expected to create a ripple effect in the rural economy of Haryana. 

By increasing fish production, it will enhance food security and nutrition for local communities. 

The scheme also aims to promote entrepreneurship among youth in the fisheries sector. 

Training and capacity-building programs will be organized to equip beneficiaries with modern aquaculture techniques. 

The PMMSY is a significant step towards achieving self-sufficiency in fish production in India. 

It is also expected to boost exports of fish and fish products from the country. 

The scheme has the potential to transform the fisheries sector in Haryana and improve the livelihoods of thousands of fish farmers. 

Overall, the construction of new grow-out ponds under PMMSY is a vital initiative for sustainable aquaculture development. 

It represents a commitment by the Indian government to support the fisheries sector and enhance the economic well-being of fish farmers. 

The implementation of this scheme will be closely monitored to ensure that the objectives are met effectively. 

The PMMSY is a comprehensive approach to addressing the challenges faced by the fisheries sector in India. 

It reflects the government's dedication to promoting sustainable development and improving the quality of life for rural communities. 

The success of the PMMSY will depend on the active participation of stakeholders, including fish farmers, cooperatives, and government agencies. 

The scheme is a promising opportunity for those involved in aquaculture to enhance their productivity and income. 

In conclusion, the PMMSY's focus on constructing new grow-out ponds in Haryana is a strategic initiative aimed at revitalizing the fisheries sector. 

It is designed to create a sustainable and profitable aquaculture industry that benefits both farmers and consumers. 

The comprehensive support provided under this scheme is expected to lead to significant advancements in fish farming practices in the state. 

The PMMSY is an essential component of India's efforts to achieve food security and economic growth through the fisheries sector.
